text:
oliver: heads up — noticed a user report where SSE client reconnects and gets a stale frame from an old session. console shows session closed but client still receives data.
katie: ugh. repro steps?
oliver: small repro: open stream -> server sends a few events -> kill pod (SIGTERM) -> client reconnects to new pod -> new pod sends cached frame matching old session id.
samir: is this the lease/conn id mismatch we've seen? sounds like routing sent request to a pod with an expired lease but the pod still had queued frames.
mira: console shows session_count dropped immediately, then +1 when reconnect happens. but user saw an event for the previous session id. weird. :confused:
oliver: yes. I think two things are happening: 1) pod reaped the session locally but didn't purge queued frames until after reconnect, 2) routing used sticky key that only checked placement index, not session_rev.
katie: do we have telemetry for frame-source session_id and session_rev? that's important to trace which pod emitted the orphan frame.
samir: currently we log session_id in stream events but not session_rev. also console event counts aggregate by route+model; we lose per-session attribution.
mira: caused a customer complaint (billing confusion) — they saw quota consumed for the orphan frame even though console showed session ended. billing + UX mismatch.
oliver: proposed fix: include `X-Session-Rev` in internal stream headers and in telemetry. routing should consider `(session_id, session_rev)` when doing sticky routing/fallbacks.
samir: agree. also we should treat queued frames as tombstoned when SIGTERM arrives. pod should atomically mark queue dead and drop frames before handing off placement.
katie: can we make a small canary: add session_rev to telemetry and console UI first (non-breaking), then change routing check in a follow-up? we want to see prevalence before changing routing behavior.
mira: add a console flag to surface "session_rev" on the streams dashboard — quick toggle for support to verify customer incidents.
oliver: priority: P1 for infra team to add header+telemetry, P2 for routing logic change, P3 for tombstone optimization.
samir: I'll draft the telemetry patch. sample header: ```X-Session-Id: abcd1234
X-Session-Rev: 5``` router check psuedocode: ```if (route.key == session_id && route.rev == session_rev) -> sticky```. 
katie: nit: keep rollout UX simple. deploy a telemetry-only canary for 1% of traffic for 2 days, then flip routing for that canary only. deploy-bot: can we schedule canary?
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: telemetry-canary -> 1% on infra-canary at 2026-03-22T02:00Z (job 9821).
mira: once canary runs, ops will check console counts and `stream.events` for orphan frames. if we still see orphan frames from pods with rev < current_rev, routing change required.
oliver: also add quick alert: streaming.orphan_frames.rate > 0.1% should page eng-platform. needs an annotation to avoid noisy pages.
samir: I'll send a PR with telemetry fields + tests and add one line to console to surface rev in the streams table.
katie: thanks. can we add a short blurb in release notes about "streaming session_rev" so support knows how to interpret it?
mira: yep will draft. tagging @support for visibility.
oliver: ok locking this thread to action items: samir telemetry PR, katie plan canary and release note, mira console toggle, samir follow-up routing PR if canary shows any orphan frames.
katie: sounds good.
samir: on it.
